review.summary: The paper introduces ISED, a neurosymbolic learning framework that uses black-box programs written in general-purpose languages (e.g., Python) to achieve higher accuracy than end-to-end neural baselines. The framework uses sampling-based gradient approximation instead of differentiable logic programming.

Demonstrates significant accuracy improvements (30%) over end-to-end neural baselines
Includes diverse benchmark tasks covering synthetic, neurosymbolic, and real-world scenarios
Provides a clear, generalizable framework for integrating structured/unstructured data

Does not compare with other non-differentiable optimization frameworks
Theoretical justification for using min/max operations as aggregators is unclear
Limited discussion of computational efficiency and scalability
